svg.title: Choose Dataflow Gen2, Copy, or Code
svg.desc: A decision and internals diagram showing when to choose Dataflow Gen2 vs Pipeline Copy vs Spark Notebooks, drilling into Dataflow Gen2's managed SQL staging engine and the critical rule not to build dependencies on internal staging artifacts.
svg.text: Transformation Decision & Dataflow Gen2 Staging Internals
Tool Selection Framework · Low-Code vs Movement vs Code · Managed SQL Staging Engine · Staging Governance

g.title: What is the dominant need? — Choose by transformation complexity and ownership rather than by connector availability alone.
g.text: Root Decision: What is the Dominant Ingestion & Transformation Responsibility?
Evaluate by transformation complexity, data scale, developer skill profile, and execution engine requirements:
A. Visual cleansing & low-code shaping ➔ Dataflow Gen2
B. High-throughput movement with minimal shaping ➔ Pipeline Copy
C. Complex algorithms, ML, or declarative SQL models ➔ Notebooks / dbt

g.title: Dataflow Gen2 — Use Power Query for visual, low-code shaping with configured destinations.
g.text: 1. DATAFLOW GEN2 (LOW-CODE SHAPING)
Visual Power Query M Shaping
• 300+ graphical transforms for business analysts
• Cleanses, pivots, enriches, and standardizes feeds
Ideal Scenarios & Strengths:
✓ Business analysts standardizing customer/sales extracts
✓ Ingesting diverse spreadsheets, CSVs, and Web APIs
✓ Automatic multi-destination publishing (Lakehouse Delta)
✓ SQL-backed scale-out staging accelerates execution
Integrated query folding diagnosis and profiling
Watch-outs & Anti-Patterns:
❌ Avoid for multi-terabyte raw bulk ingestion without shaping
❌ Complex recursive procedural loops are difficult to maintain in M
❌ Non-folding queries evaluate on single-container compute
Trap: Forcing complex streaming or ML into Dataflow Gen2
Use Spark Notebooks for ML and Eventstream for real-time.
Best Match:
Citizen data engineering, visual data preparation, and small-to-
medium tabular enrichment before landing in Lakehouses.

g.title: Pipeline Copy — Use Copy for orchestrated movement with limited transformation.
g.text: 2. PIPELINE COPY ACTIVITY (MOVEMENT)
Serverless High-Speed ELT Movement
• 100+ native connectors across multi-cloud & on-prem
• Intelligent Throughput Optimization (ITO: 4–256)
Ideal Scenarios & Strengths:
✓ High-volume multi-terabyte raw landing into OneLake
✓ Zero cluster spin-up time (instant elastic execution)
✓ ForEach fan-out across hundreds of relational tables
✓ Orchestrates multi-step dependencies & failure alerts
Fast binary file copy and Parquet compression
Watch-outs & Anti-Patterns:
❌ Cannot perform complex multi-table joins in flight
❌ Mapping transformations are limited to column renames/types
❌ Non-idempotent copy retries can cause duplicate rows
Trap: Authoring pipelines when Mirroring already supports DB
Check Mirroring source catalog first to eliminate custom ETL.
Best Match:
Raw bulk data ingestion (ELT), large file migrations, and
scheduled multi-table extraction pipelines into OneLake Bronze.

g.title: Notebook or SQL model — Use code or SQL-declarative tools for complex, testable, engine-native transformation.
g.text: 3. NOTEBOOKS & SQL MODELS (CODE-FIRST)
Code-First & Declarative Engineering
• Full PySpark, Scala, SQL & dbt transformation power
• Engine-native distributed execution in Spark / Polaris
Ideal Scenarios & Strengths:
✓ Complex algorithmic logic, graph parsing, nested JSON
✓ Machine learning feature engineering & MLflow tracking
✓ Declarative SQL modeling with dbt and version-controlled CI/CD
✓ Unit testing, modular Python packages & Git integration
Optimized Native Execution Engine (NEE) query speed
Watch-outs & Anti-Patterns:
❌ Spark cluster spin-up cold start overhead (~15-45s)
❌ Requires professional data engineering / software skillset
❌ Heavy custom maintenance overhead for simple table copy
Trap: Hand-coding Python scripts for basic database copy
Use Copy Activity for simple movement; reserve code for logic.
Best Match:
Advanced Silver-to-Gold curation, custom ML pipelines, nested
data flattening, and enterprise software engineering workflows.

g.title: Managed Gen2 staging — Dataflow Gen2 may use internal lakehouse and warehouse staging for SQL scale-out.
g.text: Dataflow Gen2 Managed SQL Staging Engine
Internal Fabric SQL Warehouse compute backing scale-out transformations
1. Staging Lakehouse & Warehouse
• Auto-provisioned in workspace
• Stages intermediate tables in Delta format
• Acts as high-speed scratch storage
2. Distributed T-SQL Execution
• Merges, joins & group-bys push down to SQL
• 10x faster than single-threaded Mashup eval
• Output streams directly to destination
How Staging Operates During a Run:
1. Mashup engine reads source data and stages it directly into `DataflowsStagingLakehouse`.
2. `DataflowsStagingWarehouse` queries the staged tables using distributed T-SQL query folding.
3. Prepared rows are committed into user's configured destination (Lakehouse Delta / Warehouse).
4. Temporary staging partitions are automatically cleaned up at the end of the refresh cycle.
Result: Scalable enterprise Power Query execution powered by Fabric capacity.

g.title: Do not own staging internals — Depending on or editing DataflowsStaging items creates an unsupported operational coupling.
g.text: CRITICAL GOVERNANCE WARNING
Do NOT Own or Depend on Staging Internals
System staging artifacts are private runtime implementation details
Strict Architectural Prohibitions:
❌ NEVER query `DataflowsStagingLakehouse` or `DataflowsStagingWarehouse` in reports.
❌ NEVER alter permissions, schemas, or delete internal staging artifacts manually.
❌ NEVER create downstream Semantic Models or Spark jobs reading staging tables.
Why This Matters & Failure Mode:
Fabric periodically recreates, renames, and drops staging tables during service updates
and schema evolutions. Any external dependency built on staging will silently break!
Golden Contract: Always point reports and downstream workloads exclusively
to the user-configured destination Lakehouse, Warehouse, or Database table.
